subject: OptimaHealth renewal: slope-adjusted commit & temporary rate shelter
messages:
From: Alejandro Santos <alejandro.santos@optimahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — rates & capacity for 2028

Ben / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking the time on Friday. We're beginning internal budgeting for calendar 2028 and need to lock the renewal numbers by the end of June. Two points from our side:

- Our usage for Q2 ended up ~35% higher than forecast; we expect sustained higher inference volume during the coming year.
- We received an internal ask to cap any list-price increase to no more than 5% YoY; procurement won't support anything beyond that without executive sign-off.

Can Redwood provide an updated renewal proposal that: (a) preserves predictable unit pricing for the first 90 days after renewal (we have an external launch in Q4) and (b) gives us a short-term cushion (credits or one-time uplift credit) for the unexpected delta from Q2?

Maria (GC) is looped for contract questions. Happy to schedule 30 mins tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Alejandro
Alejandro Santos
CFO, OptimaHealth
[optimahealth.com]


From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alejandro Santos <alejandro.santos@optimahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — rates & capacity for 2028

Alejandro — thanks for the clear ask and congrats on the product launch planning. We can absolutely structure a renewal to minimize near-term pricing shock while preserving long-term capacity economics. High-level proposal below; I attached a readable quote (Redwood_Quote_v2.pdf).

Proposal (summary):
- 12-month renewal with a slope-adjusted commit: baseline monthly commit set to current 6-month trailing average, with two scheduled step-ups (month 4 and month 8) that align to expected growth cadence.
- Temporary rate shelter: lock current unit price for first 90 days post-renewal. After day 90, standard tiered pricing resumes tied to commit bands.
- One-time grace credit: a $45,000 credit applied against the first invoice to offset the unexpected Q2 delta.
- Convertible burst pool: 10% burst capacity available for the first 120 days; bursts billed at a discounted overage rate if used.

Why this helps: the 90-day shelter gives you runway for the Q4 launch without forcing a long-term price concession; the grace credit addresses the current spike, and the slope-adjusted commit reduces the probability of large true-ups mid-year.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Kimberly to validate billing/legal language for the grace credit and burst discount.
2) If Ops approves, we'll prepare an amended order form and DocuSign packet.
3) Sign by 30 Jun to lock the temporary rate shelter.

Attachment: Redwood_Quote_v2.pdf (12 pages) — includes line-item math, commit ramp schedule, and burst rates.

Want to jump on a 20-min call tomorrow afternoon?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: Redwood_Quote_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alejandro Santos <alejandro.santos@optimahealth.com>, Maria Diaz <maria.diaz@optimahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — rates & capacity for 2028

Ben / Alejandro / Maria — reviewed the quote and the proposed constructs. A couple operational/legal items that need explicit language before we finalize: 

- Grace credit mechanics: specify whether it is a non-refundable credit applied to invoices, and whether it can be reclaimed on early termination. Recommended: non-refundable credit applied to invoice #1; no clawback unless material breach.
- Temporary rate shelter: define the exact 90-day window (calendar days from signature) and fallback pricing reference (which published tier applies after the shelter).
- Burst pool: need to set a cap on absolute GPU-hours for the 10% pool and confirm billing cadence.

I've attached a draft mutual action plan (Optima_MutualActionPlan.xlsx) with proposed signoffs and dates. Ben — I can draft the Order Form language for the grace credit and shelter as an amendment; Jordan will need to approve the extended credit.

If Optima is comfortable with those terms, I can push the DocuSign envelope with a redline of Section 4 (Billing) and the Order Form. Alejandro — can you confirm your procurement timeline (do you need POs or do we proceed with DocuSign signature only)?

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Head of Renewals — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: Optima_MutualActionPlan.xlsx (xlsx)]

Alejandro / Maria — copying final approval from my side. Reviewed Kimberly's draft and Ben's economics; here's what we can commit to for Optima: 

1) Execute 12-month Order Form with slope-adjusted commit schedule as attached.
2) Implement temporary rate shelter: current unit price fixed for 90 calendar days from signature.
3) Apply a $45,000 non-refundable grace credit to the first invoice; no clawback except in case of fraud or material contract breach.
4) Provide a convertible burst pool capped at 10% of the average monthly commit (explicit GPU-hour cap included in the Order Form). Bursts billed at 50% of the standard overage rate for the first 120 days.
5) Approval conditioned on DocuSign signature by 30 Jun to lock the shelter pricing.

Alejandro — we prepared the signed Order Form and standard amendment; DocuSign envelope is ready. Link below. If you confirm procurement is OK with DocuSign-only signature, we'll route the envelope directly to you and Maria.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/optima/opti-2027-orderform
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/OPTI-2027-0891

Ben / Kimberly — I'll push the envelope. Alejandro — thanks for the partnership — looking forward to getting you set for the Q4 launch.

Regards,
